subject: Nightingale - request for GPU advance reserve and sizing confirmation
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Sara Chen <sara@nightingale.ai>
Cc: procurement@nightingale.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Sep 2029 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Nightingale - request for GPU advance reserve and sizing confirmation

Sara / team — thanks again for a productive sync this morning. Quick summary and ask: Nightingale is approaching a late-stage decision for their inference rollout (NDG-4721). They expect a Q4 launch window and asked us for an availability guarantee for the initial ramp.

High-level ask (please):
- Confirm short-term availability for dedicated capacity: ~24 x A100-equivalent GPUs (or 48 x 80GB vRAM equivalents if tiling), for a 90-day ramp starting 2029-11-01.
- Provide an ops-level sizing read (expected sustained tokens/sec and thermal binning notes).
- If capacity exists, place a 60-day soft-hold on the slices/pods to cover the critical procurement window.

Attached: Nightingale_MVP_sizing.xlsx (their internal sizing + launch dates). I can share the HubSpot deal (NDG-4721) and a short mutual action plan after we confirm inventory.

Acceptance criteria from their side: public cloud audit (SOC2 evidence provided), SLA addendum review, and a draft MOU to sign for the soft-hold. Procurement is copied — Sara, can you confirm the expected start and whether Nightingale needs an earlier pilot footprint?

Ben / Rishi — can ops do an availability snapshot and quick thermal/tiling guidance? If we can soft-lock, Id like to capture that as a 60-day reservation (nonbinding) while legal finishes the MOU.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Sara Chen <sara@nightingale.ai>
Cc: procurement@nightingale.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Sep 2029 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightingale - request for GPU advance reserve and sizing confirmation

Karthik — thanks, I pulled a quick fleet snapshot. See attached: fleet_snapshot_sep11.pdf for an operational view. High-level notes:

- Current available headroom across US region: nominally ~30 A100-equivalent slots in 2x8 GPU pod topology through Oct/early Nov, with a stretch capacity of ~18 additional slots if we re-balance scheduled maintenance windows.
- Thermal binning: Nightingales 90-day sustained inference looks like medium-seq workloads — recommend 80GB-class nodes to avoid KV-cache fragmentation at 1k+ prompt sizes.
- Ops caveat: we have two near-term hardware reservations (internal pilot + partner POC) that are flexible but not yet released — we can discuss tradeoffs.

Questions before I commit a soft-hold:
1) Can Nightingale confirm whether they need 24 homogeneous A100s or a hybrid mix (e.g., 12x80GB + 12x40GB)? The SKU mix materially affects which pods we reserve.
2) Does the 90-day ramp require continuous throughput (24/7) or a diurnal schedule (peak windows)? That changes batching/slot sizing.

If you can confirm those two items today, I can submit a 60-day soft-hold on matching pod slots (ops sign-off pending) and draft an MOU.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Ops — Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Sara Chen <sara@nightingale.ai>
Cc: procurement@nightingale.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Sep 2029 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightingale - request for GPU advance reserve and sizing confirmation

Ben — thanks for the quick turn. Sara (and procurement) — answers inline to Ben's questions:

- SKU mix: Nightingale confirmed they prefer homogeneous 80GB-class GPUs for predictability. So 24 x 80GB nodes. (Theyll also run a small dev pilot on lower-tier pods, but for launch they want 80GB equivalents).
- Schedule: primary need is production peak hours (US PST) with 24/5 coverage initially and full 24/7 by week 6 of ramp. Expect steady sustained inference after week 4.

Sara: can you confirm via reply to procurement that the above is accurate and give an exact start date (they previously said Nov 1). Once procurement approves, Ben — we need the soft-hold submitted and a short mutual action plan (I can draft MAP and DocuSign steps).

Related: HubSpot deal NDG-4721 is updated with the sizing sheet and proposed timeline (link included below). Ive attached a one-page mutual_action_plan_nightingale.docx for ops/legal to review. If ops can lock the 24 x 80GB for 60 days starting 2029-10-01, that aligns our internal procurement and hardware staging.

Karthik
(On behalf of Nightingale team)

---
Attached: mutual_action_plan_nightingale.docx
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/NDG-4721
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Sara Chen <sara@nightingale.ai>
Cc: procurement@nightingale.ai
Date: Sat, 14 Sep 2029 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightingale - request for GPU advance reserve and sizing confirmation

Folks — ops reviewed the ask and we can place a conditional 60-day soft-hold with the following guardrails:

- Reserved capacity: 24 x 80GB-class equivalents (mapped to 3 x 8-GPU pods) across US-west region.
- Hold window: 2029-10-01 through 2029-11-30 (60 calendar days).
- Conditions: SOC2 evidence must be uploaded to our vendor portal, and procurement must acknowledge the nonbinding MOU terms within 5 business days of hold initiation.
- Ops notes: to preserve thermal balance well schedule a maintenance freeze 48 hours before planned start; ops will coordinate exact node mapping once MOU is agreed.

Im attaching a brief soft_hold_mou_draft.pdf for legal and procurement to validate. Karthik — if Nightingale signs off, confirm via reply and Ill escalate to capacity control for the formal hold ticket.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Capacity Planning — Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
